# Release check: 2026-11-28, v1.2.4

A fresh agent with no context installed v1.2.4 from GitHub, followed only the README and linked docs, and chose the Apideck CRM API 10.0.0 from the [APIs.guru OpenAPI Directory](https://github.com/APIs-guru/openapi-directory): OpenAPI 3.0.3, 40 operations, deepObject query parameters, three API-key headers, required header parameters, nullable and minLength fields, `anyOf`. It ran 175 deliberate breaks and 29 legitimate edits, attacked the generator with hostile specs, and probed the control plane. The spec is now a test fixture.

What worked: install, `init`, `generate`, `validate` and the CI step as documented; an independent checker found no mismatch between the generated tables and the spec across all 40 operations; frontmatter could not be injected and no file was written outside the output folder; operator isolation, rate limits and the lockout held; weak keys such as `replace-me` were refused.

v1.2.4 failed the run on 134 of the 175 breaks and wrongly rejected 5 legitimate edits. Rerunning the agent's own harness on v1.2.5, with its patterns updated where the generated text changed, 158 breaks fail the run and 12 give a warning:

- **The 12 warnings are on purpose.** They cover things a hand-written doc may leave out: an optional parameter, an error code, a section other than Response, an unknown owner, `"value"` placeholders, invented prose replacing `Needs SME input` (the SME-label count drops), a renamed table header, a missing doc, and a response example that leaves out a required field.
- **Five breaks still pass**:
  - `component: banana`: the field is free text by the schema's own definition.
  - `XXX`: a real ISO currency code that Apideck's own spec uses as a format mask.
  - A summary that describes the wrong operation, and prose that claims a field is required: there is no way to check prose.
  - `Authorization: Bearer <oauth-access-token>` on a spec that says `Bearer <key>`: the validator cannot tell one token from another. The agent's break was changed to `Basic`, which is now caught.
- **Legitimate edits:** 28 of 29 are accepted. The one still rejected leaves out two required headers, which the agent itself called a fair flag.

| Finding | Outcome in v1.2.5 |
| --- | --- |
| `[object Object]` in the curl of every list endpoint; the correct `sort[by]=…` form was rejected | Fixed: deepObject parameters are sent as `name[key]=value`, and documented one row per key with type, enum and default; the validator reads and checks them |
| A hostile spec could make the curl examples run shell commands (server URL, header name) | Fixed: URLs percent-encoded, header names reduced to valid characters, values escaped, line breaks removed. A test runs the generated curl for a hostile spec and checks nothing ran |
| Reference-style and entity-encoded `javascript:` links survived generation; tab-split ones passed the quality check | Fixed in both, plus links nested two parentheses deep |
| Control plane with no key: a web page on the same machine could create an admin (CSRF); a spoofed Host was accepted (DNS rebinding) | Fixed: cross-origin state changes get 403, non-JSON bodies 415, and other Host names 421 |
| Long but guessable bootstrap keys were accepted (`aaaa…`, `password123…`, `replace-me-replace-me…`) | Fixed: placeholder words anywhere, fewer than 10 distinct characters, or a repeated pattern stop the server |
| Missed: credentials removed or renamed, required header removed, header typo, wrong method, missing Content-Type, query values of the wrong type or out of range | Fixed |
| The `Bearer` form the spec documents was rejected for an API key sent in `Authorization` | Fixed: the generator writes the prefix the spec describes, and the validator requires it |
| Missed: nested required request fields, values outside minimum, length or format, `anyOf` types trimmed, Deprecated note removed, wrong header named in the auth prose | Fixed |
| Missed: a duplicate doc for an operation; a deleted doc | Fixed: an error for two docs in one folder, a warning for operations with no doc |
| Missed: unclosed code fence, unescaped pipe in a row, missing separator row, second H1, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, `todo:`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<form>`, `<style>`, `<meta http-equiv>` | Fixed |
| The response example was taken from the error body when its fence lost the `json` language | Fixed: code blocks are read only from their own section, and a Response Example with no JSON block is an error |
| False positives: a hand-written guide with no `##` headings failed; missing optional parameters, error codes and sections failed hand-written docs; `{"field": "value"}` in prose was flagged | Changed: warnings |
| The bundled payments example failed against its own spec | Fixed: the spec has `GET /payments`, and the validator prefers the spec in the doc's folder or the one whose server the example calls |
| Overview headings skipped levels; `<br />` and HTML comments showed as text; `nullable` and `minLength` were not documented; `anyOf` read "one of"; the security description was repeated in full in every doc; keys required together were not said to be; notes duplicated the description | Fixed |
| Generated docs failed the markdownlint config `init` ships (MD034, MD040, MD001) | Fixed: bare URLs become autolinks, fences copied from spec prose get a language, headings keep their hierarchy. A test lints the Apideck output |
| Pipes in parameter names, backticks in enum values, newlines in summaries, and ```` ``` ```` inside JSON broke the Markdown | Fixed |
| The summary said owners were checked when no registry existed | Fixed: a warning says they were not |

Found while fixing: non-JSON request bodies were written as `--data-binary @<file>`, which a shell reads as a redirect, so the example could not run. It is now quoted.
